kept.title: Win11 caption/border color matched to theme (seamless chrome)
kept.description: Today the title bar is whatever DWM picks: near-black (#1F1F1F-ish) in dark mode vs the client's RGB(32,32,32), and plain white in light mode vs the client's RGB(243,243,243) — a visible seam at the caption line, worst in light mode. Win11 22000+ lets us paint the caption, its text, and the window border exactly: DWMWA_CAPTION_COLOR (35), DWMWA_TEXT_COLOR (36), DWMWA_BORDER_COLOR (34). Implementation: in FANCONTROL::ApplyTheme the dwmapi module and DwmSetWindowAttribute pointer are already loaded at fancontrol.cpp:769-780 — right after the existing attr-20/19 immersive-dark call, add three more pSet calls passing COLORREF values that mirror the brush palette built at lines 751-760 (caption = dlgbg, text = m_clrText, border = RGB(58,58,58) dark / RGB(216,216,216) light). Do the same in the static ApplyDarkToDialog (fancontrol.cpp:710-720), which is already invoked for the Settings dialog (2807, 2906) and Curve editor (3159), so all three windows get a unified 'borderless' Win11 look. On pre-22000 builds DwmSetWindowAttribute returns E_INVALIDARG for these attributes — simply ignore the HRESULT; the existing attr-20 dark caption remains the fallback. No struct/typedef changes needed (the PFNDWMSWA signature already takes LPCVOID). This is the lightweight alternative to Mica: a real Mica backdrop (DWMWA_SYSTEMBACKDROP_TYPE) would require the client area to stop painting opaque WM_CTLCOLOR brushes — a heavy rewrite — so it is deliberately rejected.
kept.where: fancontrol.cpp ApplyTheme (lines 767-780, palette at 751-760), ApplyDarkToDialog (lines 707-742)
kept.os_requirement: Windows 11 build 22000+; on Windows 10 the new attributes fail harmlessly and the existing immersive-dark (attr 20/19) caption is kept
kept.implementation_notes:
Insertion point 1 — FANCONTROL::ApplyTheme, fancontrol.cpp inside the `if (pSet)` block, immediately after line 777 (the attr-19 fallback): declare COLORREF caption = dlgbg; COLORREF captext = this->m_clrText; COLORREF border = this->DarkMode ? RGB(58,58,58) : RGB(216,216,216); then pSet(this->hwndDialog, 35, &caption, sizeof(caption)); pSet(this->hwndDialog, 36, &captext, sizeof(captext)); pSet(this->hwndDialog, 34, &border, sizeof(border)); — fire-and-forget, no FAILED() checks. Do NOT fold these into the existing FAILED(attr20)->attr19 chain; keep them as independent calls after it. The `if (this->hwndDialog)` guard at line 767 already protects the early ApplyTheme() call at fancontrol.cpp:149 (window not yet created).

Insertion point 2 — static ApplyDarkToDialog, fancontrol.cpp inside the `if (pSet)` block after line 717. One correction to the proposal's wording: this is a static free function taking only (HWND, BOOL dark) — it has no access to m_hbrDlg/m_clrText, so it cannot literally 'mirror the brush palette'; duplicate the same RGB literals derived from `dark` (caption = dark ? RGB(32,32,32) : RGB(243,243,243); text = dark ? RGB(235,235,235) : RGB(32,32,32); border = dark ? RGB(58,58,58) : RGB(216,216,216)). The codebase already accepts this kind of literal duplication (severity palette exists in 4+ places), but a tiny file-static helper, e.g. ApplyDwmChromeColors(HWND, BOOL dark), called from both sites would keep them in sync and stay well under the LOC budget.

Minor optional nicety: if you ever want to return to system-default chrome (not needed since the app always forces dark or light), pass DWMWA_COLOR_DEFAULT (0xFFFFFFFF). Not required for this change.

Use plain integers 34/35/36 with comments, matching the existing style of hardcoded 20/19 (the project does not include a modern dwmapi.h SDK guarantee).

kept.title: Follow system dark/light theme (DarkMode=2 auto + live ImmersiveColorSet switch)
kept.description: DarkMode is hardcoded to default 1 (fancontrol.cpp:113) and only changes via the 7012 checkbox or ini; the app never reacts when Windows switches theme (e.g. scheduled auto-dark). Add an 'auto' setting: (1) keep this->DarkMode as the effective 0/1 used by all ~12 existing consumers, add int DarkModeSetting (0/1/2) next to it in fancontrol.h:169; (2) ini: extend the existing parse at misc.cpp:611-614 to store DarkModeSetting and write it back via the config table at misc.cpp:36; (3) add a small QuerySystemDark() helper that reads HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize\AppsUseLightTheme with RegGetValueA (returns dark=1 if the value is missing, matching today's default) — do NOT use uxtheme ordinal 132 ShouldAppsUseDarkMode, because ApplyTheme already calls SetPreferredAppMode ForceDark/ForceLight (fancontrol.cpp:793) which skews ord 132's answer; (4) in FANCONTROL::DlgProc add a case WM_SETTINGCHANGE next to the WM_DPICHANGED case at fancontrol.cpp:2517: if DarkModeSetting==2 and mp2 points at the ANSI string "ImmersiveColorSet" (this is an MBCS build, so lParam arrives as char*), recompute QuerySystemDark(), and if it differs from DarkMode set it, call ApplyTheme(), and resync checkboxes 7012 (main) and 9306 (Settings) with BM_SETCHECK; (5) the interactive toggles at fancontrol.cpp:2291 and 2942 set DarkModeSetting=DarkMode (explicit override), preserving current behavior exactly when the user picks a mode by hand. Optionally expose auto in the Settings checkbox grid as a 'Follow system theme' checkbox (new id 9327 next to 9301-9324) that writes DarkMode=2. The window, menus, and both modal dialogs then flip live with the OS theme — matching every modern Win11 app.

(2) misc.cpp:611-614 — parse into DarkModeSetting with a clamp (values <0 or >2 → treat nonzero as 1; today any nonzero atoi result is dark, so preserve that for 0/1 and reserve exactly 2 for auto); derive 'this->DarkMode = (DarkModeSetting==2) ? QuerySystemDark() : (DarkModeSetting!=0);' AFTER ReadConfig returns at fancontrol.cpp:256 and before InitThemeAndChrome at 275 (not inside the line parser — Fahrenheit-style ordering bugs lurk if other keys follow). Also decide whether the default-ini template line 'DarkMode=0' at misc.cpp:732 should become 2 for new installs. (4) New 'case WM_SETTINGCHANGE:' beside fancontrol.cpp:2517: guard 'if (this->DarkModeSetting==2 && mp2 && _stricmp((const char*)mp2, "ImmersiveColorSet")==0)' (mp2 is NULL for many broadcasts — NULL-check is mandatory); recompute QuerySystemDark(), and only if it differs set DarkMode, call ApplyTheme(), and resync 7012 with the existing one-liner pattern from fancontrol.cpp:882/2999. Do not set rc=TRUE; fall through returning FALSE like other unhandled broadcasts. (5) Explicit-override paths: after fancontrol.cpp:2291 and after fancontrol.cpp:2942 add 'this->DarkModeSetting = this->DarkMode;' (and if the optional 9327 'Follow system theme' checkbox is added to dialog 9300 at res/FanControl.rc:178-218, read it before 9306 in ApplySettingsFromDialog and skip the override when checked; seed it at WM_INITDIALOG near fancontrol.cpp:2777). (6) CORRECTION to the proposal: the main DlgProc cannot BM_SETCHECK 9306 because the modal Settings dialog hwnd is not stored (ShowSettingsDialog fancontrol.cpp:3061-3065). Two options: (a) minimal — drop that step; 9306 is re-seeded from this->DarkMode at every WM_INITDIALOG (fancontrol.cpp:2777), so a freshly opened dialog is always right, and an open one keeps its stale theme until closed; or (b) live-flip — add the same WM_SETTINGCHANGE case to SettingsDlgProc (fancontrol.cpp:2762-2921) and CurveDlgProc (3142-3239); both are top-level owned windows and receive the broadcast themselves; they should call QuerySystemDark() directly (broadcast delivery order between windows is unspecified, so do not assume this->DarkMode was already updated by the main window) then ApplyDarkToDialog(hwnd, dark) (fancontrol.cpp:710-720) + InvalidateRect + CheckDlgButton(9306). Option (b) is ~15 extra lines and makes the 'dialogs flip live' claim true. kept.title: Dark, flat Win11-rounded tooltips (drop XP balloon style)
kept.description: Every tooltip is created WS_POPUP|TTS_ALWAYSTIP|TTS_BALLOON (AddTip fancontrol.cpp:483-486; AddDialogTip ~635-642 for Settings/Curve), so a dark-mode user gets bright-white XP-era balloon bubbles popping over a dark window — the most visibly legacy chrome remaining. Fix in two strokes: (1) delete TTS_BALLOON from both CreateWindowEx calls — a one-token change that restyles all ~40 registered tips at once; a plain themed tooltip automatically gets the modern flat look and rounded corners on Win11; (2) theme the tips dark using the exact pattern already in ThemeChildProc (fancontrol.cpp:658-675): AllowDarkModeForWindow(ord 133)(hTip, true) then SetWindowTheme(hTip, L"DarkMode_Explorer", NULL) when dark, SetWindowTheme(hTip, NULL, NULL) when light (the proven Notepad++/WinMerge dark-tooltip recipe; SetPreferredAppMode is already set at fancontrol.cpp:793 so the dark theme class resolves). The main window's shared m_hwndTip is a WS_POPUP owned window, not a child, so the EnumChildWindows theming pass misses it — re-theme it explicitly inside ApplyTheme's existing uxtheme block (near fancontrol.cpp:797-801) so toggling the 7012 checkbox restyles tips live. AddDialogTip's tips are created after ApplyDarkToDialog runs and are recreated per dialog invocation, so a single themed call at creation suffices there (read self->DarkMode, already available in SettingsDlgProc/CurveDlgProc). If the ordinal or theme call fails (pre-1809 Win10), tips remain standard flat light tooltips — still a visual upgrade over balloons.

kept.title: Fade in/out on tray hide/show (AnimateWindow AW_BLEND)
kept.description: Hiding to tray is currently a two-step jolt: ShowWindow(SW_MINIMIZE) (WM_CLOSE fancontrol.cpp:2454, tray menu 5030 at 2360, tray left-click toggle 2624/2648) plays the genie minimize animation toward a taskbar button that doesn't exist (WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW has none), then WM_SIZE/SIZE_MINIMIZED hides abruptly (2508-2510); restore (2340-2342, 2619-2621, 2643-2645) snaps in with zero transition. Add FANCONTROL::ShowMainWindow(bool show): for hide, when MinimizeToSysTray is set call AnimateWindow(hwndDialog, 150, AW_HIDE|AW_BLEND) directly (skipping the SW_MINIMIZE round-trip entirely), else keep SW_MINIMIZE; for show, call AnimateWindow(hwndDialog, 150, AW_BLEND), then the existing SetForegroundWindow + PostMessage(WM__GETDATA) refresh. AnimateWindow returns FALSE on failure — fall back to plain ShowWindow in that branch so behavior can never regress. Replace the six call sites listed above plus the startup show at fancontrol.cpp:466. AnimateWindow lives in user32 (already linked, available since Win2k) so no guard is needed; AW_BLEND renders dialog children correctly on Win8+. Result: the most frequent interaction with this tray app — toggling the window — gets the soft fade Windows 11 users expect instead of a teleport.

kept.title: Segoe UI Variable (Text/Display) with runtime fallback across the whole font stack
kept.description: Every CreateFontA site hardcodes 'Segoe UI' and the tray text icon uses Tahoma; on Windows 11 the app should adopt the system's variable optical faces. Add a ~12-line face picker: static BOOL CALLBACK FaceExistsProc(...) {*(BOOL*)lp=TRUE; return FALSE;} plus PickUiFace(const char* want) that fills LOGFONTA.lfFaceName, calls EnumFontFamiliesExA on a screen DC, and returns want if found else 'Segoe UI'. Use 'Segoe UI Variable Text' for m_hFontDlg/m_hFontHdr/m_hFontBig and 'Segoe UI Variable Display' for the 12pt m_hFontTitle (display optical size for large text, per the Win11 type ramp) in both font-build sites: InitThemeAndChrome (fancontrol.cpp:845-853) and RescaleForDpi (fancontrol.cpp:1382-1393). Crucially, also create m_hFontDlg at startup in InitThemeAndChrome and push it with the existing EnumChildWindows(SetFontChildProc, ...) pattern (today that push only happens after a DPI change at fancontrol.cpp:1394-1395), because the .rc template FONT statement cannot express a fallback face — this is what gets checkboxes, radios, edits, the log and the RichEdit onto the Variable face. Do the same one-liner push in SettingsDlgProc and CurveDlgProc WM_INITDIALOG so the modal dialogs match. Finally swap dynamicicon.cpp:192 'Tahoma' for the picked face (and bump lfWeight 400->600 at dynamicicon.cpp:184 in the size>16 branch so 2-digit tray temps read heavier), keeping the 'Small Fonts' <=16px branch untouched.
kept.where: fancontrol.cpp InitThemeAndChrome (845-865), RescaleForDpi (1378-1407), SettingsDlgProc/CurveDlgProc WM_INITDIALOG; dynamicicon.cpp:183-198 (GetFont); new static helpers next to SetFontChildProc (fancontrol.cpp:1350)
kept.os_requirement: Any supported Windows; Segoe UI Variable is only picked when installed (Win11 build 22000+), older systems get exactly today's Segoe UI via the face-existence probe
kept.implementation_notes: Corrections/insertion points: (1) In InitThemeAndChrome, create m_hFontDlg alongside the others (insert after fancontrol.cpp:853) and add the matching delete-guard next to 842-844; do the EnumChildWindows blanket push BEFORE the existing hdr/big/title override pushes at 854-865 (mirror RescaleForDpi's order at 1394-1407) and before ReflowLayout() at 897 so design geometry is captured with the final font. (2) The proposal's PickUiFace as a static next to SetFontChildProc (fancontrol.cpp:1350) is invisible to dynamicicon.cpp — either declare it non-static in a shared header (fancontrol.h) or duplicate the ~12-line probe locally in dynamicicon.cpp; the latter avoids header churn. (3) For SettingsDlgProc/CurveDlgProc, prefer NOT to reuse self->m_hFontDlg directly: it is sized at the main window's DPI while the modal lays out at its own DPI under PMv2. Safer ~10-line variant per dialog: WM_GETFONT -> GetObjectA(LOGFONTA) -> swap lfFaceName to the picked face -> CreateFontIndirectA -> EnumChildWindows push, DeleteObject on WM_DESTROY. If reusing m_hFontDlg anyway, guard for NULL (it is now non-NULL after the startup fix, but keep the guard). (4) GDI variable-font caveat worth knowing, not a blocker: GDI exposes Segoe UI Variable named instances as separate families, so FW_SEMIBOLD against family "Segoe UI Variable Text" maps to the nearest real weight (regular/bold) — the same quirk the existing "Segoe UI"+FW_SEMIBOLD code already has, so it is behavior parity. Same applies to the dynamicicon lfWeight 400->600 bump (GDI may embolden synthetically at tray-icon sizes — visually fine for digits). (5) RescaleForDpi face strings at 1384/1387/1390/1393 must use the same picker so a DPI change does not silently revert to plain Segoe UI; cache the picked faces once (static) rather than re-enumerating per call.

kept.title: Flicker-free interactive resize: WS_EX_COMPOSITED during size-move + WM_ERASEBKGND + no-erase invalidate
kept.description: Every WM_SIZE tick ends with InvalidateRect(NULL, TRUE) (fancontrol.cpp:1326), so drag-resizing erases and repaints 17 controls plus the dialog background each frame — visible flash/tear, worst in dark mode. Three small fixes: (1) add WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE / WM_EXITSIZEMOVE cases next to the existing WM_SIZE case (fancontrol.cpp:2507): on enter, SetWindowLong(hwnd, GWL_EXSTYLE, GetWindowLong(hwnd, GWL_EXSTYLE) | WS_EX_COMPOSITED) so USER double-buffers the whole child tree during the drag; on exit, clear the bit and do one final InvalidateRect (keeping it transient avoids any steady-state cost). (2) add a WM_ERASEBKGND case in DlgProc: FillRect((HDC)mp1, &clientRect, this->m_hbrDlg); rc = 1; — guarantees the background is erased in the theme color in one pass instead of the dialog-manager default, removing the light flash in dark mode (m_hbrDlg already exists, fancontrol.h:184). (3) change the ReflowLayout tail invalidate (1326) and the ApplyTheme full invalidate (822) to bErase=FALSE since WM_ERASEBKGND/WM_CTLCOLOR now paint everything. Also add WS_CLIPCHILDREN to the slim dialog templates 9001/9003 which lack it (res/FanControl.rc lines 79 and 154) for parity with 9000/9002.
kept.where: fancontrol.cpp DlgProc near WM_SIZE (2507-2515): new WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE/WM_EXITSIZEMOVE/WM_ERASEBKGND cases; ReflowLayout (1326); ApplyTheme (822); res/FanControl.rc lines 79, 154
kept.os_requirement: WS_EX_COMPOSITED works on XP+; under DWM (Vista+) it is nearly free. No guard needed
kept.implementation_notes: Implement a TRIMMED version: (1) In FANCONTROL::DlgProc, add two cases adjacent to WM_SIZE (after fancontrol.cpp:2515): 'case WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE:' → SetWindowLongPtr(hwnd, GWL_EXSTYLE, GetWindowLongPtr(hwnd, GWL_EXSTYLE) | WS_EX_COMPOSITED); rc = TRUE; break; and 'case WM_EXITSIZEMOVE:' → clear the bit the same way, then ::InvalidateRect(hwnd, NULL, TRUE); rc = TRUE; break. (2) Append WS_CLIPCHILDREN to the STYLE lines of templates 9001 and 9003 (res\FanControl.rc:79 and 154). DO NOT implement the proposed item (3): leave InvalidateRect(..., TRUE) untouched at fancontrol.cpp:1326 and 822 — bErase=FALSE breaks theme-toggle background repaint (background is painted only during erase via the WM_CTLCOLORDLG brush, fancontrol.cpp:2085-2087) and degrades the programmatic-resize paths (ApplyLogVisibility 913-939, RescaleForDpi) that run outside ENTER/EXITSIZEMOVE; the composited buffer already absorbs the erase flash during drags. DO NOT implement item (2)'s WM_ERASEBKGND handler — it duplicates the existing WM_CTLCOLORDLG-driven erase color and adds nothing; if it were ever added, note the proposal's return convention is wrong for a dialog proc: WM_ERASEBKGND is not a direct-return message, so it would need SetWindowLongPtr(hwnd, DWLP_MSGRESULT, 1) plus returning TRUE, not just 'rc = 1'. Net change: ~12-15 lines in fancontrol.cpp plus 2 words in the .rc — well under the proposal's 25-line estimate once the two incorrect sub-fixes are dropped. Note WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE also fires for title-bar moves; the transient composited bit is harmless there.

kept.title: System accent color for non-semantic emphasis: 'On' state word + section headers (DwmGetColorizationColor)
kept.description: All emphasis colors are hardcoded and the app ignores the user's Windows accent color entirely (zero hits for DwmGetColorizationColor/AccentColor in the repo): the owner-drawn title line colors the 'On' state word a fixed RGB(0,170,0) green (fancontrol.cpp:1959), and the bold section headers use plain m_clrText. Win11's design language uses the accent for active/on states and personalized emphasis. Implementation: tiny helper COLORREF GetAccentColor(COLORREF fallback) near ApplyDarkToDialog (~line 705): LoadLibraryA("dwmapi.dll"), GetProcAddress("DwmGetColorizationColor") — the same guarded dynamic-dwmapi pattern as the existing dark-titlebar code at fancontrol.cpp:769-780 — convert the ARGB to COLORREF; in dark mode, if luminance ((2*r+5*g+b)/8) < 80, blend 40% toward white so a near-black accent stays readable on the RGB(32,32,32) dialog. Cache the result in a new m_clrAccent member refreshed in ApplyTheme (747-760, where m_clrText is set), and add a 'case 0x0320:' (WM_DWMCOLORIZATIONCOLORCHANGED, define locally like WM_DPICHANGED at fancontrol.cpp:26-28) in DlgProc that re-derives it and invalidates — live update when the user changes their accent. Consumers, all non-semantic so the severity color language stays intact: (a) the WM_DRAWITEM 8115 branch swaps RGB(0,170,0) for m_clrAccent (fancontrol.cpp:1959); (b) WM_CTLCOLORSTATIC returns m_clrAccent for the bold section-header statics 9210/9198/9199/9201/9202 (slim: 9220/9221) and the bold LTEXT headers in SettingsDlgProc (2864-2891, excluding severity-colored 9315-9317) and CurveDlgProc (3186-3203); (c) the trackbar custom-draw idea reuses the same member for its channel fill. Skip accent entirely when high contrast is on. Fallback when the API is missing or fails: the existing green / current header color — identical to today.

(4) New `case 0x0320:` (define WM_DWMCOLORIZATIONCOLORCHANGED locally next to WM_DPICHANGED at fancontrol.cpp:26-28) in the DlgProc switch — anywhere among the existing cases, e.g. after the WM_DPICHANGED case at 2517-2521 — re-derive m_clrAccent (wParam already holds the new ARGB) and InvalidateRect the header statics + 8115 (or whole window, matching ApplyTheme:822). (6) Consumer (b): in the WM_CTLCOLORSTATIC block at 2089-2116, after `int cid = ::GetDlgCtrlID(...)` (2094), add `else if (cid==9210||cid==9198||cid==9199||cid==9201||cid==9202||cid==9220||cid==9221) txt = this->m_clrAccent;` — keep it AFTER the 8100/8103 severity branch so severity wins. (7) Settings/Curve headers: only feasible if the IDC_STATIC LTEXTs at res/FanControl.rc:183,189,192,198,206,210 (and Curve 226,230-233 if desired) get real IDs first (e.g. 9340-9345) plus matching branches in SettingsDlgProc 2874-2878 / CurveDlgProc 3192 — about 10 extra lines across .rc+cpp; otherwise omit the modal dialogs and the idea still stands. kept.title: Win11-style manual-fan trackbar via NM_CUSTOMDRAW (accent channel fill, round thumb)
kept.description: The msctls_trackbar32 slider 8311 is the most dated-looking control left: in dark mode ThemeChildProc gives it the classic Win95 theme (fancontrol.cpp:671, the L"",L"" branch), and even in light mode it's the stock XP-era thumb. Modernize it with standard trackbar custom draw — no subclassing, no owner-draw rewrite. DlgProc currently has NO WM_NOTIFY case (verified: zero hits repo-wide), so add one: if ((NMHDR*)mp2)->idFrom == 8311 && code == NM_CUSTOMDRAW, switch on NMCUSTOMDRAW.dwDrawStage: CDDS_PREPAINT -> result CDRF_NOTIFYITEMDRAW; CDDS_ITEMPREPAINT with dwItemSpec == TBCD_CHANNEL -> FillRect the full nmcd.rc with m_hbrDlg, then draw a centered 4px-high RoundRect bar: the portion left of the thumb (split point from TBM_GETTHUMBRECT) filled with m_clrAccent (from the accent idea, or RGB(0,120,212) fallback), the remainder RGB(96,96,100) dark / RGB(198,198,198) light; result CDRF_SKIPDEFAULT; TBCD_THUMB -> Ellipse filled with the accent color (+1px m_hbrDlg-colored inner border for the Win11 ring look) inside nmcd.rc; result CDRF_SKIPDEFAULT; TBCD_TICS -> CDRF_SKIPDEFAULT. Critical dialog-proc detail: BaseDlgProc returns rc directly (fancontrol.cpp:1746-1784), so the CDRF_* value must be set via SetWindowLongPtr(hwnd, DWLP_MSGRESULT, result) and rc = TRUE returned, or the stages never fire. Also remove the slider from the classic-theme exclusion in ThemeChildProc (apply L"",L"" still — custom draw replaces all parts, so the base theme no longer matters). Pure paint code; the WM_HSCROLL fan-level logic (2009-2040) is untouched.
kept.where: fancontrol.cpp DlgProc: new case WM_NOTIFY (insert near WM_DRAWITEM, ~1922); ThemeChildProc (661-675) comment update; reuses m_clrAccent / m_hbrDlg (fancontrol.h:184-186)

kept.title: Flicker-free log append with EM_REPLACESEL instead of full rewrite
kept.description: Trace() rewrites the entire 9200 log edit on every line: GetDlgItemText of up to 8KB, strcat, SetDlgItemText, EM_SETSEL, EM_LINESCROLL 9999 (misc.cpp:1087-1119) — full-control repaint, caret churn and visible flicker per log line whenever the log panel is open, plus O(n) text shuffling on a 1-2s timer cadence. Replace with append-in-place: HWND hLog = GetDlgItem(hwndDialog, 9200); int len = GetWindowTextLength(hLog); SendMessage(hLog, EM_SETSEL, len, len); SendMessage(hLog, EM_REPLACESEL, FALSE, (LPARAM)line); — the edit control repaints only the new line and auto-scrolls. Enforce the 100-line cap by deletion from the top only when needed: int lines = SendMessage(hLog, EM_GETLINECOUNT,...); if (lines > 100) { int idx = SendMessage(hLog, EM_LINEINDEX, lines-100, 0); wrap in WM_SETREDRAW FALSE/TRUE: EM_SETSEL(0, idx); EM_REPLACESEL(FALSE, ""); then InvalidateRect(hLog,...); } and re-seat the caret at the end. The file-logging block (misc.cpp:1106-1114) and line formatting stay as-is; the 8KB stack buffer and the backwards line-counting loop (1078, 1092-1103) are deleted. Net visual result: the log streams smoothly with zero flash, matching the repaint-churn-avoidance work already done for the readouts (SetDlgTextIfChanged in fanstuff.cpp).
kept.where: misc.cpp FANCONTROL::Trace (1074-1120): replace the GetDlgItemText/strcat/SetDlgItemText/EM_SETSEL/EM_LINESCROLL block
kept.os_requirement: none — plain edit-control messages, all Windows versions
kept.implementation_notes: Insertion point: replace misc.cpp:1087-1103 (GetDlgItemText/strcat/backwards line loop) and misc.cpp:1116-1119 (SetDlgItemText/EM_SETSEL/EM_LINESCROLL) inside FANCONTROL::Trace; keep the line formatting (1078-1085, shrink the 8192 'trace' buffer away) and keep the Log2File block (1106-1114) unconditional. Required corrections to the proposal: (1) Raise the text limit: change EM_LIMITTEXT 4096 to a larger value (e.g. 0x7FFF or 16384) at BOTH fancontrol.cpp:269 and fancontrol.cpp:316 — EM_REPLACESEL respects EM_LIMITTEXT (WM_SETTEXT does not), so without this the append path stalls at 4096 chars before the 100-line cap engages. Alternatively trim from the top whenever GetWindowTextLength + strlen(line) would exceed the limit. (2) NULL-guard: HWND hLog = GetDlgItem(this->hwndDialog, 9200) is NULL on slim dialogs 9001/9003 (no 9200 control, res/FanControl.rc:79-175) and during early startup; do the file-log write first, then 'if (!hLog) return;'. (3) Suggested order: append first (EM_SETSEL(len,len) + EM_REPLACESEL(FALSE, line)), then if EM_GETLINECOUNT > 100, WM_SETREDRAW FALSE, EM_SETSEL(0, EM_LINEINDEX(lines-100)), EM_REPLACESEL(FALSE, ""), EM_SETSEL(end,end), WM_SETREDRAW TRUE, InvalidateRect(hLog, NULL, FALSE) — trimming only fires once per line after the window fills, and ES_AUTOVSCROLL makes EM_REPLACESEL scroll the caret into view, so EM_LINESCROLL 9999 is deleted (optionally send EM_SCROLLCARET after the trim re-seat). (4) Also update the now-wrong comment at misc.cpp:1076-1077 about the 4096 cap / 8KB buffer. Send messages via the cached hLog (SendMessage) rather than SendDlgItemMessage to avoid repeated lookups; all messages are plain-edit messages, no new headers or libs.

kept.title: 32bpp alpha rounded-badge text tray icon (Segoe UI digits, per-rebuild DPI size)
kept.description: The temperature tray icon becomes a Win11-style rounded color badge with antialiased Segoe UI digits and transparent corners, instead of the current hard-edged square built from CreateCompatibleBitmap + a monochrome mask (dynamicicon.cpp:24-42, 141-143) with 'Small Fonts'/Tahoma faces (dynamicicon.cpp:189-198). Implementation: in the CDynamicIcon constructor replace iconBmp_ with CreateDIBSection (BITMAPINFOHEADER: biBitCount=32, negative biHeight, keep the pvBits pointer), zero the bits, build the badge with CreateRoundRectRgn(0,0,w+1,h+1,w/3,h/3) + FillRgn using the existing severity brush switch (lines 44-77), draw the text as today, then do one post-pass over the DWORD pixel array setting alpha 0xFF000000 for pixels where PtInRegion is true and 0 elsewhere (~600-1600 px, runs at most 2x/sec and only when the rebuild-skip in TaskbarTextIcon.h:25-30 misses). Keep ICONINFO but pass a dummy 1bpp CreateBitmap(w,h,1,1,NULL) as hbmMask — the shell uses the per-pixel alpha. In CDynamicIcon::CreateFont drop the bitmap-face branch: always 'Segoe UI', lfWeight=600, ANTIALIASED_QUALITY (not ClearType — subpixel rendering corrupts the alpha channel). Also stop freezing the size at construction (TaskbarTextIcon.h:113 m_iconSize): re-query GetSystemMetrics(SM_CXSMICON) inside _createdicon each rebuild and add it to the skip-signature (m_lastFarbe block), so a DPI change regenerates the icon; the existing WM_DPICHANGED handler (fancontrol.cpp:2517-2521) just adds a RemoveTextIcons() call to force it. For symbol-icon mode, swap the two LoadImage calls in TASKBARICON::Construct/SetIcon (winstuff.cpp:154-156, 238-240) for LoadIconMetric(hInstRes, MAKEINTRESOURCEW(id), LIM_SMALL, &h) — comctl32 v6 is already linked and manifested.
kept.where: dynamicicon.cpp constructor + CreateFont; TaskbarTextIcon.h _createdicon/m_iconSize; winstuff.cpp TASKBARICON::Construct/SetIcon; fancontrol.cpp WM_DPICHANGED handler (~2517)
kept.os_requirement: Vista+ (32bpp alpha tray icons work since XP; LoadIconMetric is Vista+, matching the app's existing _WIN32_WINNT 0x0600 floor in _prec.h:6). No runtime guard needed.
kept.implementation_notes: Insertion points confirmed: dynamicicon.cpp constructor (replace lines 28-42 bitmap/mask setup; keep brush switch 44-77; alpha post-pass after text draw at ~line 130, BEFORE DeleteObject(rgn) at line 133 since PtInRegion needs the live HRGN); CDynamicIcon::CreateFont (replace 189-198 with single Segoe UI/600/ANTIALIASED_QUALITY branch); TaskbarTextIcon.h _createdicon (re-query size at top, add m_lastSize next to m_lastFarbe/m_lastFont at line 83 and to the skip test 25-30); fancontrol.cpp:2519 (add this->RemoveTextIcons() beside RescaleForDpi); winstuff.cpp:153-156 and 238-240 (LoadIconMetric swap). Corrections: (a) the dummy mask CreateBitmap(w,h,1,1,NULL) has UNINITIALIZED bits — pass a zeroed buffer instead, since low-color/RDP render paths can still consult the mask; keep it in iconMaskBmp_ so the destructor at dynamicicon.cpp:149 frees it, and delete the now-dead memDC2_/oldBmp_2 mask-prep code (26-27, 30-39, 83-84, 137-138). (b) GDI text on a DIB section writes 0 into alpha bytes, so the region post-pass (alpha=FF inside, full 0x00000000 outside for premultiplied consistency) is mandatory, exactly as proposed; ClearType must indeed stay off. (c) DPI caveat: in a PMv2 process GetSystemMetrics(SM_CXSMICON) returns system-DPI metrics, not per-monitor, so the WM_DPICHANGED + per-rebuild re-query combo only picks up system-DPI changes (primary-display scale / sign-in DPI), not the main window moving between monitors — acceptable since the taskbar lives at the primary/system DPI, but don't expect per-monitor behavior; GetDpiForSystem (runtime-loaded, Win10 1607+) would be a slightly better source if desired. (d) LoadIconMetric returns HRESULT with HICON out-param — guard with SUCCEEDED and fall back to the existing LoadImage call on failure, matching the codebase's runtime-guard style. (e) Use BI_RGB, biPlanes=1, negative biHeight as proposed; select the DIB into memDC1_ exactly where iconBmp_ is selected today (line 31).

kept.title: NOTIFYICON_VERSION_4 tray protocol: keyboard activation + menu anchored to the icon
kept.description: Upgrades the Win2k-era tray callback protocol. Visually/UX: the context menu pops exactly at the icon (shell-supplied anchor point) instead of the raw cursor position, Shift+F10/Enter/Space on the keyboard-focused tray icon work like clicks, and the rich multi-line tooltip keeps working via NIF_SHOWTIP. Implementation: in TASKBARICON::Construct (winstuff.cpp:142-181) drop the hand-rolled NOTIFYICONDATAV5 oversize-cbSize trick — at _WIN32_WINNT 0x0600 plain NOTIFYICONDATA is already the Vista-size struct — add NIF_SHOWTIP to uFlags, and after a successful NIM_ADD set nof.uVersion=NOTIFYICON_VERSION_4 and call Shell_NotifyIcon(NIM_SETVERSION,&nof), recording success in a new m_trayV4 flag; same two lines after the NIM_ADD loops in CSystemTray::Create (SystemTraySDK.cpp:257-261) and AddIcon (299-311). In FANCONTROL::DlgProc WM__TASKBAR (fancontrol.cpp:2612-2733) change switch(mp2) to switch(LOWORD(mp2)) (compatible with both protocols since WM_* < 0x10000), add cases NIN_SELECT/NIN_KEYSELECT falling through to the existing show/hide code at 2616-2625, and add case WM_CONTEXTMENU that builds POINT{GET_X_LPARAM(mp1),GET_Y_LPARAM(mp1)} (v4 passes anchor coords in wParam) and hands it to the existing menu body — factor lines 2652-2729 into a ShowTrayMenu(POINT*) helper; MENU::Popup already accepts a POINT* (winstuff.cpp:482-489). Keep the WM_RBUTTONDOWN case as the fallback path, gated on !m_trayV4 so v4 mode doesn't double-pop the menu.
kept.where: winstuff.cpp TASKBARICON::Construct/SetTooltip; SystemTraySDK.cpp Create/AddIcon; fancontrol.cpp WM__TASKBAR handler 2612-2733 (+ new ShowTrayMenu helper)
kept.os_requirement: Vista+ for NIM_SETVERSION/V4; if NIM_SETVERSION fails the m_trayV4 flag stays false and the legacy WM_RBUTTONDOWN/WM_LBUTTONDOWN path is used unchanged.
kept.implementation_notes: Corrections to the proposed approach: (1) DOUBLE-TOGGLE BUG: under NOTIFYICON_VERSION_4 the shell still delivers the mouse messages (WM_LBUTTONDOWN, WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK, WM_RBUTTONDOWN, with anchor coords in wParam) IN ADDITION to NIN_SELECT/NIN_KEYSELECT/WM_CONTEXTMENU. The proposal gates only WM_RBUTTONDOWN on !m_trayV4; the WM_LBUTTONDOWN case (fancontrol.cpp:2616-2625) and WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK case (2640-2649) must be gated the same way, otherwise every left click toggles show/minimize twice (WM_LBUTTONDOWN then NIN_SELECT) for a net no-op flash. Also note NIN_KEYSELECT arrives twice for Enter (shell quirk; once for Space) — debounce with GetMessageTime or only act on NIN_SELECT+NIN_KEYSELECT once per tick. (2) NIF_SHOWTIP must persist across NIM_MODIFY, not just NIM_ADD: add it to TASKBARICON::SetTooltip uFlags (winstuff.cpp:275), SetIcon (winstuff.cpp:237), SetBalloon (winstuff.cpp:301), CSystemTray::SetTooltipText (SystemTraySDK.cpp:521), CSystemTray::SetIcon (~SystemTraySDK.cpp:370), AddIcon (SystemTraySDK.cpp:304), and include it in m_uCreationFlags so InstallIconPending's re-add inherits it (SystemTraySDK.cpp:251, 952). (3) NIM_SETVERSION must follow every successful NIM_ADD: placing it in TASKBARICON::Construct covers the RebuildIfNecessary/TaskbarCreated rebuild (fancontrol.cpp:1771-1778 recreates via Construct), but CSystemTray also re-adds in InstallIconPending (SystemTraySDK.cpp:946-961, reached from OnTaskbarCreated at 773-776 via the hidden window) — add the two lines there too. (4) GET_X_LPARAM/GET_Y_LPARAM are not available in fancontrol.cpp: _prec.h does not include windowsx.h (only dead WCE-ifdef'd code in SystemTraySDK.cpp:824-827 references it); either add #include <windowsx.h> to _prec.h or use (short)LOWORD(mp1)/(short)HIWORD(mp1). (5) Flag plumbing: TASKBARICON can expose m_trayV4 next to UpAndRunning/osVersion (winstuff.h:67-77, accessible via this->pTaskbarIcon), but the text icon's CSystemTray is buried inside CTaskbarTextIcon (protected m_pSystray, TaskbarTextIcon.h:74) with no accessor — simplest is a single FANCONTROL-level bool set after icon creation (fancontrol.cpp:423/2348/3015 and ProcessTextIcons ~3416), since only DlgProc consumes it; otherwise add a one-line getter on CTaskbarTextIcon. Insertion points otherwise as proposed: NIM_SETVERSION after winstuff.cpp:169-174 NIM_ADD, after SystemTraySDK.cpp:257-261 and 305; switch(LOWORD(mp2)) at fancontrol.cpp:2614; ShowTrayMenu(POINT*) factored from fancontrol.cpp:2652-2729 passing the point through to m.Popup (currently no-point call at 2728). kept.title: UIPI fix: tray icon actually survives Explorer restarts when elevated
kept.description: The app runs requireAdministrator (res/xp-manifest.txt:13), so the medium-integrity Explorer's 'TaskbarCreated' broadcast is silently blocked by UIPI — the careful re-add code in BaseDlgProc (fancontrol.cpp:1756-1779) and CSystemTray::WindowProc (SystemTraySDK.cpp:899-901) never fires, and since the main window is WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW (no taskbar button), an Explorer crash/restart currently leaves the app unreachable with no icon at all. Fix: one process-wide allow — GetProcAddress(GetModuleHandleA("user32.dll"), "ChangeWindowMessageFilter") and call it with (s_TaskbarCreated, 1 /*MSGFLT_ADD*/) right after the RegisterWindowMessage("TaskbarCreated") at fancontrol.cpp:1760 (process-wide covers CSystemTray's hidden WS_POPUP window too). Visible result: kill/restart explorer.exe and both the symbol and text tray icons reappear within one 500ms timer tick instead of vanishing forever.
kept.where: fancontrol.cpp BaseDlgProc WM_INITDIALOG block (1756-1761)
kept.os_requirement: Vista+ (ChangeWindowMessageFilter); GetProcAddress-guarded no-op if absent, behavior unchanged.
kept.implementation_notes: Insert inside the existing WM_INITDIALOG block in BaseDlgProc, immediately after s_TaskbarCreated = RegisterWindowMessage("TaskbarCreated") at fancontrol.cpp:1760: typedef BOOL (WINAPI *PFNCWMF)(UINT, DWORD); PFNCWMF pFilter = (PFNCWMF)::GetProcAddress(::GetModuleHandleA("user32.dll"), "ChangeWindowMessageFilter"); if (pFilter) pFilter(s_TaskbarCreated, 1 /*MSGFLT_ADD*/);. Notes/corrections: (a) this spot is correct - it executes before the This==NULL guard at 1763-1765, so the filter is installed at first dialog creation, before timer 2's first ~500ms tick creates the CTaskbarTextIcon/CSystemTray hidden window (fancontrol.cpp:2206-2208 -> 3416), and re-execution on a dialog recreate (slim/full swap, fancontrol.cpp:278-327) is idempotent; (b) ChangeWindowMessageFilter is process-wide, so no per-HWND ChangeWindowMessageFilterEx plumbing into SystemTraySDK.cpp is needed; (c) do NOT count on CSystemTray::OnTaskbarCreated for the visible recovery - InstallIconPending early-returns when m_bShowIconPending is FALSE (SystemTraySDK.cpp:948), which it is after any previously successful NIM_ADD; the recovery that actually restores the icon is BaseDlgProc's own handler at fancontrol.cpp:1767-1778; (d) user32.dll is guaranteed loaded in this GUI process, so GetModuleHandleA (not LoadLibrary) is fine and leak-free; (e) test in the default text-icon mode (ShowTempIcon=1) while elevated: taskkill explorer.exe + restart - without the fix the icon never returns; with it the symbol icon returns immediately in the handler and the text icon on the next 500ms tick; (f) soften the changelog claim for symbol mode, which already self-heals via winstuff.cpp:250-251/282-285.

kept.description: All balloons today are bare NIIF_INFO, so Win11 renders the toast with the generic blue 'i' and ignores focus-assist etiquette (winstuff.cpp:293-313 TASKBARICON::SetBalloon; SystemTraySDK.cpp:583-631 ShowBalloon; call sites fancontrol.cpp:1010/1040 Game-mode, 2183 + 3422-3429 startup hints). (2) TASKBARICON::SetBalloon (winstuff.cpp:293-313): after line 302 set nof.dwInfoFlags |= NIIF_USER|NIIF_LARGE_ICON|NIIF_RESPECT_QUIET_TIME and nof.hBalloonIcon = LoadIconMetric(hInstRes, MAKEINTRESOURCEW(this->IconId), LIM_LARGE, ...)
